sections.heading: Biography
sections.text: Dr. Chung is an Assistant Professor in Statistics and Data Science at the University of Central Florida. He received his Ph.D. and M.S. in Statistics from the University of Georgia as well as M.B.A. in Finance and B.B.A. from Korea University. His research interests include aggregating with regularization, developing efficient algorithms for graphical model, and estimating conditional dependencies through precision matrices for brain network analysis. His application work focuses on interdisciplinary research collaborations with pure and applied mathematicians, computer scientists, psychologists and neuroscientists.

sections.heading: Biography
sections.text: Dr. Hsin-Hsiung “Bill” Huang is a Professor of Statistics and Data Science at the University of Central Florida (UCF) and a U.S. citizen of Taiwanese American heritage. He earned his Ph.D. in Statistics from the University of Illinois at Chicago, an M.S. in Statistics from the Georgia Institute of Technology, an M.S. in Mathematics from National Taiwan University, and dual B.A./B.S. degrees in Economics and Mathematics, also from National Taiwan University.

sections.heading: Biography
sections.text: His research has been supported by multiple grants from the National Science Foundation’s Algorithms for Threat Detection (ATD) program, for which he has served as Principal Investigator, including NSF DMS-1924792 and DMS-2318925. He has also served as Principal Investigator on a Lockheed Martin research project involving anomaly detection in high-dimensional missile simulation data. His biomedical research is supported by the National Institutes of Health (NIH), where he serves as Principal Investigator of a National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) R01 award (1R01AI206603-01) focused on Bayesian phenotyping, multilayer network inference, and epidemic intelligence for sexually transmitted infections. He also serves as a Co-Investigator on a National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) R01 award (1R01NS133094-01A1).

sections.heading: Biography
sections.text: Larry Tang is a statistician specializing in statistical methodology and collaborative research. His current methodological research areas include statistical methods in forensics, diagnostic medicine, group sequential designs and substance abuse research and criminology.  He received his Ph.D. in Statistics from Southern Methodist University in 2005. He did postdoctoral training in the Department of Biostatistics at University of Washington. His research is currently supported by National Institute of Justice and National Institutes of Health.

sections.heading: Biography
sections.text: Dr. Zhang received his Ph.D. in Statistics from the University of Alberta, Canada. Before joining UCF in 2015, he served as Assistant and Associate Professor of Statistics at the University of Alaska Fairbanks, and later as Associate and Full Professor of Statistics at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln. During his tenure at Nebraska, he also worked as a Mathematical Statistician at the National Cancer Institute (NCI), where he developed the CI*Rank website ( https://surveillance.cancer.gov/cirank/ ), an important tool providing ranked, age-adjusted cancer incidence and mortality rates by U.S. state, county, and special regions. This platform continues to support researchers, policymakers, and the public in assessing community health and healthcare policies.

sections.heading: Research
sections.text: My research focuses on the function and evolution of endosymbiotic organelles in land plants, and applications for plant biotechnology. I have a particular interest in the role of plastid (chloroplast) and mitochondrial genomes in shaping plant physiology. I use a variety of techniques, including genomics, transcriptomics, molecular evolution approaches, molecular cloning, chlorophyll fluorometry, and protein biochemistry.  I enjoy mentoring researchers at all levels, from undergraduate to post-doctoral. If you are interested in joining my lab, please reach out to me via email.

sections.heading: Biography
sections.text: Weixuan Xia is a tenure-track Assistant Professor in Mathematics at the University of Central Florida. Previously, he was an Assistant Professor (RTPC) of Mathematics at the University of Southern California. He received his Ph.D. in Mathematical Finance from Boston University and served as a Finance Teaching Fellow at MIT Sloan. Dr. Xia’s research spans quantitative finance and applied probability, particularly integrating stochastic modeling and machine learning to address optimization and game-theoretic problems arising in economics and finance. His recent work has focused on multi-criteria optimization and set-valued stochastic systems, subject to path-dependence and jumps.

sections.heading: Biography
sections.text: Dr. Alexandria “Lexie” Orozco is a bioarchaeologist with a biocultural approach to understanding our human past via the integration of biological, geospatial, and quantitative methods. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Central Florida and holds graduate certifications in GIS from the University of Texas at Dallas and the University of Central Florida. Her research considers identity, diet, health, and mobility in the past via geospatial and stable isotopic analysis of skeletal tissues (carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen) and mortuary contexts. Recent work is focused on the diet of a Migration period population from Plinkaigalis, Lithuania and Sai Island, Sudan. Her postdoctoral research focused on radiocarbon dating, the development of a head mounted cultural heritage AR application as a part of the DATCH (documenting and Triaging Cultural Heritage) project, and the development of 3U satellites in conjunction with a multidisciplinary team at UCF. At Oxford College of Emory University she supervised student-led research focused on NAGPRA repatriation and historic cemetery restoration.
